key_insight: SrTiO3-xHx oxyhydrides strongly favor a cis O4H2 anion arrangement, and the predicted ordering depends sharply on the DFT+U choice, with U = 3.3 eV serving as an HSE06-like proxy.
engineering_relevance: Accurate anion-order predictions in perovskite oxyhydrides require calibrated energetics, because the favored hydride arrangement can affect structural stability, migration behavior, and device-relevant defect chemistry.
method: Built a cluster expansion for SrTiO3-xHx using HSE06 hybrid-DFT energetics as the training benchmark.
Compared DFT+U mixing/ordering energies across U values to identify U = 3.3 eV as the best HSE06 proxy.
Used ground-state searches and Monte Carlo sampling to assess long- and short-range anion ordering.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports up to ~100 meV/anion variation in mixing energies across DFT+U settings and a ~200 meV per hydride stabilization for the cis O4H2 configuration.
watch_item: Ordering conclusions are highly sensitive to the chosen DFT+U parameter, so uncalibrated U values can mis-rank configurations and distort cluster-expansion predictions.
paper_title: Long- and Short-Range Anion Order in SrTiO$_{3-x}$H$_x$ Perovskite Oxyhydrides: DFT+$U$ Sensitivity and HSE06 Cluster Expansion
